approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecular graph. It samples local atom and bond edits, including direct exchanges of an aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing carbon in the same six-member ring. Valid, canonically fresh neighbors pass through a short-lived inverse-motif memory before filling the announced batch. The walk moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when that score is worse than its source, breaks exact score ties by canonical spelling, and keeps a separate best archive. Each selected transition installs at most four inverse local-motif restrictions. Installation first reserves up to two slots for each sign, then fills any remaining slots by occurrence-change magnitude and canonical motif order. A candidate is vetoed only if it matches both inverse signs from the same selected transition. Overlapping keys take the latest provenance and deadline, entries expire after four completed steps, and a documented oldest-entry release handles generation obstruction. Normalized canonical identities preserve the proposal-to-feedback join.
approach.novelty: Remove the sign reservation from the four-slot installation choice. Select the four highest-ranked changed motifs using the Parent's existing magnitude and canonical ordering, irrespective of how many have each sign. Keep insertion order unchanged whenever the selected keys agree with the Parent. This isolates the contribution of sign-balanced memory allocation to a veto that already requires both signs. Earlier siblings changed which motifs rank first while retaining the sign reservation, changed matching or memory lifetime, or removed the whole veto or nitrogen-relocation menu. None removed this reservation alone. The Parent trace suggests that most changed selections would still retain both signs, so the utility prediction is non-inferiority, not stronger chemical credit or a guaranteed reduction in vetoes. Actual memory and admission changes will establish execution; complete scored trajectories will test that prediction.

hypothesis: Remove the per-sign reservation from bounded inverse-motif installation: select up to the inherited four changed motifs by the Parent's global descending absolute occurrence-change and canonical-motif rank without sign quotas, preserving inherited insertion order on coincident selections and retaining the same-transition bidirectional veto and memory lifecycle.

finding_summary.headline: Removing sign balance changed search and lost 0.01185 in mean endpoint score
finding_summary.insights: Keeping both signs available is not enough to preserve the contribution of balanced memory allocation. Which motif representatives inherit each transition’s provenance matters even when capacity, magnitude ranking, veto logic and memory lifetime stay fixed. Ten relaxed admissions produced only one source improvement, one tie and eight losses, with no immediate archive gains; most changed the batch cutoff without becoming the next state. Conversely, one added veto enabled an oxygen-deletion refill that did improve the zaleplon archive. These opposing local effects show why fewer vetoes cannot stand in for better search. The loss supports retaining the quota in the developed method on this panel, while leaving the responsible individual replacements unresolved: ten conditional comparison batches lack a tenth recorded member, and passive memories do not define independently evolved walks or scores. Chemistry remained in the same aromatic/carbonyl, aryl-amine and sulfur-cage families, with nearly unchanged size and persistent reactive heteroatom bonds and unspecified stereochemistry. The observed score tradeoff therefore does not establish improved chemical feasibility.
finding_summary.results: The removal executed exactly and changed 116 of 420 memory installations that could affect later proposals. Most still retained both signs: 414 of 420, while total selected motif-change magnitude increased by only one count. On the Child’s recorded history, restoring balanced selection would change twelve gate decisions: ten candidates were newly admitted by the removal and two were newly vetoed. This reached actual scored allocation and selected states. Eight of fifteen task/seed trajectories changed; all fifteen finished. The three-seed mean final Top-1 score fell from 0.521759 to 0.509908, a paired loss of 0.011851 that exceeds the allowed 0.002 decline. Seed effects were +0.009516, -0.041309 and -0.003760. Sitagliptin supplied the largest loss, especially seed 1 at -0.195597, and DRD2 also declined; zaleplon improved. Mean recorded AUC fell from 0.393354 to 0.391556. The mechanism is confirmed, and the non-inferiority prediction is rejected.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyls and aryl amines persist, with reactive N/O bonds, unusual sulfur coordination and densely fused cages
molecular.overall_character: Every supplied child and parent trajectory was read, and all requested tasks are covered. Each task contains 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. The proposal ring-closure-token rate is 1.0 throughout, aromatic-token rates range from 0.7977 to 1.0, and mean SMILES lengths range from 46.3 to 70.1. These are molecular string readings rather than fractions of aromatic atoms or tests of chemical stability. The output consists of substantial ring-bearing compounds: indole/benzofuran amides and aryl ketones, bulky decorated aza-heterocycles, halogenated aryl amines, bridged nitrogen/carbonyl systems and highly fused sulfur cages. Distinct seed families give moderate structural diversity, while the strongest excerpts remain concentrated in closely related frameworks. Typical heavy-atom sizes are unchanged from parent n-abcd951ab7cc, and 7 of the 15 task/seed trajectories are identical. Changed trajectories retain the same broad chemistry and its unresolved liabilities rather than showing uniformly more conventional structures. Ordinary amides, amines, ethers and carbonyls coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, N-N/N-O bridges, peroxides, sulfur-halogen bonds and multiply bonded sulfur with additional substituents or hydrogen. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0. Neutral strings do not establish solution protonation, and unassigned configurations do not imply achiral structures. Size and structural counts below are passive RDKit readings of supplied SMILES; no new oracle score, synthesis score or geometric-feasibility result was generated. Local score associations do not reveal an unseen required scaffold or prove that chemically questionable bonds are necessary.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 21-29 heavy atoms. The strongest families combine fused aromatic or partly unsaturated rings with an aryl amide or aryl ketone. The leading benzofuran-like carboxanilide bears methyl groups, thiol, an amino-chloromethyl group and an N-chloro amide. Another strong molecule is a comparatively ordinary ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide. The changed seed-0 leaders are indene-like aminopyridyl ketones bearing methoxy and N-fluoroaminomethyl substituents, with optional carbon-bound fluorine. Their aromatic nitrogen chemistry is clearly present. Low molecules enlarge or interrupt the fused ring system, lose aromatic organization or replace the carbonyl connection. The ordinary amide and ketone fragments are plausible synthetic motifs, while the reactive nitrogen substituents and dense bridged derivatives make the full set questionable.
liabilities: N-Cl amide, N-F/N-O groups and amino-chloromethyl functionality are distinct concerns from ordinary aryl halogenation.
Thiols, dense ring closures and unusual sulfur connections occur in alternative families.
Late bridged molecules add N-N functionality and further ring complexity without defining configuration.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

finding_summary.headline: Removing sign balance changed search and lost 0.01185 in mean endpoint score
finding_summary.insights: Keeping both signs available is not enough to preserve the contribution of balanced memory allocation. Which motif representatives inherit each transition’s provenance matters even when capacity, magnitude ranking, veto logic and memory lifetime stay fixed. Ten relaxed admissions produced only one source improvement, one tie and eight losses, with no immediate archive gains; most changed the batch cutoff without becoming the next state. Conversely, one added veto enabled an oxygen-deletion refill that did improve the zaleplon archive. These opposing local effects show why fewer vetoes cannot stand in for better search. The loss supports retaining the quota in the developed method on this panel, while leaving the responsible individual replacements unresolved: ten conditional comparison batches lack a tenth recorded member, and passive memories do not define independently evolved walks or scores. Chemistry remained in the same aromatic/carbonyl, aryl-amine and sulfur-cage families, with nearly unchanged size and persistent reactive heteroatom bonds and unspecified stereochemistry. The observed score tradeoff therefore does not establish improved chemical feasibility.

approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecular graph. It samples local atom and bond edits, including direct exchanges of an aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing carbon in the same six-member ring. Valid, canonically fresh neighbors pass through a short-lived inverse-motif memory before filling the announced batch. The walk moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when that score is worse than its source, breaks exact score ties by canonical spelling, and keeps a separate best archive. Each selected transition installs at most four inverse local-motif restrictions. Installation first reserves up to two slots for each sign, then fills any remaining slots by occurrence-change magnitude and canonical motif order. A candidate is vetoed only if it matches both inverse signs from the same selected transition. Overlapping keys take the latest provenance and deadline, entries expire after four completed steps, and a documented oldest-entry release handles generation obstruction. Normalized canonical identities preserve the proposal-to-feedback join.
